citations.anchor: serves exactly what it did before the plugin existed
citations.why: Deletes every audience, then asserts a public read still returns the entry — if the scope emitted a fragment with an empty catalogue the total would drop.

citations.anchor: defaults an entry with no row to visible
citations.why: Asserts the emitted fragment contains COALESCE( and , true), which is exactly the default-visible clause the invariant names.

citations.anchor: reads an empty allow list as everyone, not as nobody
citations.why: canRead with allow: [] admits both the anonymous reader and a tagged one; inverting the rule fails both assertions.

citations.anchor: refuses a denied reader even when they are also allowed
citations.why: A reader in both lists is refused, and a reader in allow-only is admitted — the deny-wins precedence.

citations.anchor: hides a restricted entry from a reader in no segment
citations.why: An anonymous read of an entry with a non-empty allow returns total 0; a special-case branch admitting the tagless reader would make this 1.

citations.anchor: checks the deny list, then the empty-allow case, then the intersection
citations.why: Asserts the emitted SQL carries NOT (, cardinality(, = 0 OR and && — the three canRead rules in that order.

citations.anchor: drops a target the reader cannot see from BOTH items and total
citations.why: A relation expansion over two linked tags, one restricted, must answer items length 1 AND total 1 — the exact both-fields claim. (REST only; no GraphQL/MCP equivalent exists.)

citations.anchor: binds the whole list as a single parameter
citations.why: Counts the Param chunks of the fragment and asserts exactly one holding the whole array — an inlined or per-id expansion fails it.

citations.anchor: offers an unscoped audience in every workspace
citations.why: An audience created with no workspaceIds is returned by GET /api/segments?workspace= for two different workspaces; reading empty as none would return 0.

citations.anchor: counts an entry opened back up as open
citations.why: accessRestricted is 'has an entry_access row'; after a save of two empty lists the entry must match accessRestricted=false, which only holds if the writer deleted the row rather than blanking it.

citations.anchor: reads a missing list as empty rather than refusing it
citations.why: Stored allow ['s1'] plus a payload naming only deny leaves allow [] — a merge would have kept 's1'.

citations.anchor: applies a decision to every language of the record
citations.why: Access written on the English row is read back on its German sibling, so the write covered the whole locale group.

citations.anchor: rolls the whole save back on a malformed payload
citations.why: A create whose extensions.access is malformed 400s and leaves total 0 — the entry insert is undone, which only happens if the extension ran on the save's own transaction.

citations.anchor: refuses a caller who may edit the record but not decide who reads it
citations.why: A caller holding only content:update is rejected with ForbiddenException and no write happens; the sibling test in the same file pins the no-op exemption.

citations.anchor: refuses a caller it cannot identify
citations.why: Builds the extension over a principal store whose current() returns undefined and asserts ForbiddenException rather than a pass.

citations.anchor: records the access of a save that never mentioned it
citations.why: A PATCH that carries no access key still produces a revision whose snapshot.extra.access holds the stored lists — capture ran on a save that did not touch access.

citations.anchor: refuses a restore that would change who can read the entry
citations.why: A payload differing from the stored access, from a caller without segments:manage, is refused — while the neighbouring test shows a matching one is allowed.

citations.anchor: appends a revision on every sibling it rewrote
citations.why: A decision written on one language must add a revision to the sibling row it rewrote; the 'exactly one revision' test in the same describe pins the deduplication half.

citations.anchor: reaches a translation created after the decision
citations.why: A translation created after the entry was restricted reads back the group's audiences, so the create's own extension pass inherited them.

citations.anchor: never leaves a segment in both lists
citations.why: withState over an access already naming the id on both sides leaves it in exactly one; the withStates describe carries the same assertion for the bulk path.

citations.anchor: ignores order, so a reordered list is not a pending change
citations.why: sameAccess over two allow lists differing only in order returns true — the staging's pending-change test; the server-side copy is pinned in packages/segments/domain/src/lib/entry-access.spec.ts.

citations.anchor: sends nothing about access when nothing was staged
citations.why: Saves an entry without opening the Access tab and asserts the captured save body's extensions is undefined — the access key is not sent at all.

citations.anchor: keeps a decision on an audience the list no longer shows
citations.why: With a stored decision on an audience the workspace-scoped directory no longer returns, the counter names it and the save body still carries its id in allow.

citations.anchor: reads back what it just restricted
citations.why: content_access_get answers restricted: true on an entry the same token just closed — a reader-scoped entry read would have hidden it from itself.

citations.anchor: is a copilot-only propose tool gated on segments:manage
citations.why: Asserts effect 'propose', surfaces ['copilot'] and requires ['segments:manage'] on content_propose_access; agent-access.spec.ts pins its absence from the MCP catalogue.

citations.anchor: offers no tool over the audience directory, at any scope
citations.why: Enumerates the tool catalogue under a full token and asserts no segments_create/update/delete/set name appears.

citations.anchor: re-checks the grant rather than trusting the proposal
citations.why: The applier over an empty granted-slug set throws Unknown content type and never reaches setForGroup; the neighbouring test pins that the accepted path goes through setForGroup.

citations.anchor: throws rather than silently skipping a table with no id
citations.why: A context whose table has no id column makes scope() throw /has no "id" column/ instead of returning undefined.

citations.anchor: answers an entry id that exists nowhere the same way
citations.why: Pins the identical-404 half of the boundary check; the two neighbouring tests assert a foreign entry id is refused on both the open-up and the restrict path with the other workspace's row untouched.

citations.anchor: refuses more audiences on one side than an entry may hold
citations.why: 201 ids in extensions.access.allow 400s and leaves total 0 — the cap is applied on the DTO-less entry-save path.

segments:I-09.reason: canRead(access, readerSegmentIds) is handed neither a workspace nor the catalogue (packages/segments/domain/src/lib/entry-access.ts:50), so there is no input a harness could vary to observe it consulting isOfferedIn. The absence is enforced by the signature, not by an assertion.
